A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MENTOR research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I. Both have 19 pages; extracted text and rendered pages 2–19 are identical. Differences are confined to first-page attribution and version information.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation experiments on DMC, Meta-World and Adroit, physical-robot results, and appendix ablations and analyses. Figure 6 and Table 1 report learning curves and robot-task success rates.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation and physical-robot results in Figure 6 and Table 1, together with the original experiments and analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The MoE policy backbone, task-oriented perturbation mechanism and load-balancing objective are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same simulation tasks, three physical-robot tasks, multitask combinations and disturbance scenarios in Section 4 and the appendices.

E2.justification: DrM, DrQ-v2, ALIX and TACO retain the same participation in the reported comparisons. The MLP/MoE controls and MENTOR ablation variants are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training budgets, real-world rollout counts, model configurations and testing procedures are unchanged in Section 4, Table 1 and Appendices B–E.

E4.justification: Both retain identical component ablations, expert-number/top-k sensitivity tests, gradient-conflict analyses, expert-utilization studies and disturbance demonstrations, including the appendix evidence.

E5.justification: The simulation experiments still report four random seeds. Figure 6 retains standard-deviation shading for DMC and success-rate ranges for Meta-World and Adroit; no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged, including Figure 6's benchmark curves, Table 1's robot success rates, and the appendix ablation and time-efficiency results in Tables 2, 5 and 6.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1–2.2, the MoE and perturbation equations, the load-balancing formulation, and the appendix efficiency and reward definitions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same architectural and optimization contributions and the same sample-efficiency and performance claims, including the reported 83% versus 32% real-world success comparison.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, pretrained-encoder interpretation, computational-efficiency limitation in Appendix E and applicability limitations in the conclusion are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, camera inputs, reward functions, reset procedures and the experimental-video access link are unchanged, including Appendices A–E and Tables 3–4.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning are identical, including Section 5's discussion of visual RL and parameter perturbation.

P1.justification: v3 adds a dagger beside Zhengrong Xue and the footnote text 'Student advisor,' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The research prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added advisor marker slightly shifts the first-page author line and reflows the affiliation/correspondence footnote; the margin stamp also changes. All figures and tables are unchanged, and rendered pages 2–19 are identical.

improvement.justification: v3 adds an advisor attribution and updates version information, with only localized first-page reflow. The scientific content and evidence, including all appendices, remain identical. These administrative edits do not meaningfully alter the paper's evidential support, reproducibility or readability.
